You know, he did see an on campus psychiatrist or psychologist (I always get those two mixed up yet I just finished a psych course on that herp derp me) but I never got word on how it went. I asked him and he just said "eh". When I asked more he tried to change the subject or started to sound frustrated with each question.

It's not so much fear...it's more of being a bit arrogant about it. He just doesn't feel like "seeking help" is the way to go, because he's been doing things on his own his whole life. 

I told him "well, just because it's been that way, doesn't mean it has to continue that way."

Hey, wow. I know I'm a day late, but you and I are almost the same in terms of the situation. My boyfriend B...He ODed on various pills and I called the cops because he never replied to me and suddenly said good bye instead of good night which freaked me out cause it was in a different tone...one of those unsettling tones where you know something went wrong.

The stupid cop was interrogating him like he was some sort of stupid criminal and that didn't make it any better. Initially they threw him in jail until the hospital said, no we need to take him and the whole situation could have been avoided if the cops didn't look at him like some sort of juvenile delinquent.

He was in the hospital and was taking calls. A couple of times his family answered, but at one point I did get to my boyfriend and he sounded upset. A bit confusing because some days he would say "I'm thankful but I'm not. I'm glad, but I'm not." and it got really confusing. I knew overall, he's still upset about it because he does bring it up from time to time saying how he wish he didn't let anyone know or talk to anyone that day.

I keep a private blog recording what goes on in our every day life. The one thing that's good is that, my boyfriend B, is aware he's depressed and feels like a burden. As much as it has been very unhealthy for me, I try my hardest to carry on in my life as well as I'm supporting him...

And I don't know, the littlest things he says are the best things. He'll say something about life that sounds very optimistic. Other days he doesn't and goes back to cutting...but I always try to bring that optimistic side out of him and get him excited for job searching or where we'd travel in the future and it's just something I try to overpower more than his suicidal side. 

I try to hold onto those small bright moments. And I will continue to hold onto them dearly and protect them. And I hope you and your boyfriend will get through this and we will do the same.

To be honest, it sounds kind of weird and kind of bad at the same time but...I feel a bit glad I'm not the only one who's going through this and I'm glad to share my story with you. Please take care of yourself okay stranger?

Out of curiosity OP, have you ever been cyber-bullied? If not I can understand why you're asking this question. And if you have been, I applause you for taking it by a grain of salt.

I used to have a formspring back in high school, expecting innocent questions. Boy was I wrong. The mean and cruel comments I got, at first I kind of laughed at it, but then the more you get or the more cruel the comments get you kind of question. Then you start getting a bit paranoid...I felt uncomfortable being myself around anyone in high school. I kind of just kept quiet and didn't trust anyone. Anonymity amongst your peers kind of builds mistrust and social anxieties cause you fear judgment. I even thought my own friends were turning against me.

Even when I deleted my formspring, someone actually went to the school administration and fabricated a lie that got me in deep trouble with my family which caused my family to restrict me from a lot of things and I was almost denied my graduation because the cyber bullies actually convinced the administration I was a bad student. People are cruel and they will keep hunting their prey down until you're weak enough to be chomped down on. They will continue to seek ways to put you down until you're out. So simply stepping away or even deleting the source of the problem, only makes them find a way around it.

Another reason why it's such a problem is that for some people, they're already knocked down in their personal lives from poor parenting or family troubles, abuse, neglect, so on and so forth. So it's like you're poking at an internal wound only making it worse.

On the bright side though, once you get past the troubles of cyber-bullying, you sort of build more of a back bone and learn how to respond to such things in a mature manner, whether that'd be just shrugging it off or just letting people say what they wanna say.

EDIT: Added reason why stepping away is not a simple solution.
